> **WIP — Draft PR.** This work will receive further updates. It is not ready to merge; the known numerical difference and remaining validation are documented below.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 consumer indexer layers rescore the candidate blocks selected by a source layer before selecting their own attention indices. On SM90, the compact Triton scorer remains a significant decode cost: in the batch-64 measurement below, candidate scoring takes 21.18 ms of a 107.35 ms GPU decode round.

This PR adds a CUDA implementation of `fp4_index_logits_candidates` for SM90. It reads the existing paged FP4 cache directly and produces scores in the existing compact candidate order. In the measured Triton 3.6 configuration, candidate scoring is 4.50× faster and the complete GPU decode round is 15.89% shorter. Against Triton 3.7.1, CPU-observed steady decode round intervals fall by a median 6.24% across three batch-32 pairs and by 9.03% in one batch-64 pair. Output throughput also depends on speculative acceptance and serving load.

This work continues the existing candidate-block workflow: source layers publish candidate blocks, and consumer layers score only those blocks. SM100 already uses this workflow through its DeepGEMM sparse backend. Building on [#40860](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40860), which provides compact Triton candidate scoring on SM90, this PR adds a dedicated SM90 CUDA scorer to reduce candidate-scoring overhead during decode/verify.

The rebased #40860 dependency is kept in a separate commit; the CUDA implementation and tests are another commit. Once the upstream base contains the dependency, the remaining change should be the CUDA increment. All performance comparisons below already include the rebased #40860 implementation in the Triton baseline.

## Modifications

- Add a JIT-compiled CuTe/CUDA scorer for SM90 BF16 queries with 32 heads, head dimension 128, and compression ratios 1 and 2, with Triton fallback for unsupported configurations.
- Score compact candidates directly from the existing paged FP4 cache, using natural D128 BF16 MMA, optimized FP4 decoding, Q/weight reuse, and register-based head reduction.
- Preserve the existing input/output and candidate-selection interfaces, and add numerical, masking, layout, dispatch, downstream top-k/finalizer, and CUDA Graph replay tests.

The CUDA path preserves the existing BF16 rounding sites and scale flush-to-zero behavior. Natural D128 accumulation changes the floating-point accumulation order relative to the parity-split Triton implementation; bitwise-identical scores and selections are not guaranteed for every input.

## Accuracy Tests

Post-rebase validation completed with **227 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed**, plus 14 passing subtests, using normal package initialization with Torch 2.13.0+cu129 and Triton 3.7.1; GPU tests ran on H20 SM90. Validation ran at `2ec60be9ab`, whose source tree is identical to submitted revision `c604e9712c`; both are based on main `8368f86fd7`. CUDA computation is preserved; submission cleanup updates test registration and formatting. Performance results remain tied to the benchmark revisions stated below.

| Coverage | Result |
|---|---:|
| CUDA scorer, dispatch, and independent oracle controls | 109 passed |
| Hopper backend replay through the default entry point | 8 passed |
| Candidate protocol and BF16 candidate scorer regressions | 101 passed |
| Upstream balanced-versus-per-row paged graph replay | 4 passed |
| Candidate graph-variant factory regressions | 5 passed, plus 14 subtests |

The numerical reference decodes the same quantized inputs independently with CPU PyTorch FP64, preserves the specified BF16 conversions, and propagates fixed FP32 accumulation bounds through the dot product and head reduction. It checks finite scores against those bounds and checks masks exactly. Top-512/top-1024 checks cover selection cutoffs and the actual downstream consumer/finalizer; they are separate from score-error checks.

In a separate migration check on Torch 2.9.1+cu129/Triton 3.5.1, six fixtures comprising 18,336 scores matched the original CUDA implementation through `65f7b9f` bit for bit. The real downstream top-k/finalizer produced identical final indices for CUDA and Triton on those six fixtures. This establishes the checked migration behavior, not universal CUDA/Triton equivalence.

**Known numerical difference:** an earlier saved fixture, case 065, has a one-candidate replacement in the actual top-1024 selected set relative to the frozen historical Triton baseline. It remains unresolved and was not rerun as part of the 227-test post-rebase suite. Case 058 has a strict `torch.topk` diagnostic difference but matching actual consumer selected sets. The historical 66-shape/594-state sweep was not repeated during integration. Separate diagnosis of five score outliers located their differences at BF16 dot-product rounding boundaries; those five inputs had matching final indices, but do not clear case 065.

No model task-accuracy or log-probability equivalence result is claimed. The known selection difference needs a numerical-acceptance decision supported by model-level validation, or an implementation change, before merge.

<details>
<summary>Integration test selection</summary>

Run from the CUDA checkout in the matching SM90 environment:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -x \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_candidate_index_logits_cuda.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_candidate_dispatch_cuda.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_candidate_contract_cpu.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_candidate_cuda_dispatch.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer.py::test_hopper_indexer_backends_replay \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer.py::test_fp4_paged_logits_balanced_matches_per_row_replay \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_triton_candidate_indexer.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_candidate_bf16_mqa.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv41_candidate_graph_variants.py
```

Recorded validation ran the CPU and GPU selections separately with a wrapper to capture environment metadata and failure tensors. Exact commands, environments, JUnit results, and source hashes are retained with the evidence.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8×H20, TP8, Torch 2.13.0+cu129/CUDA 12.9. Humming, DSpark block size 5 with adaptive speculation disabled, overlap scheduling, bounded replay, and decode CUDA Graphs remain enabled. Workloads use random token IDs, 24,576 input tokens and 500 output tokens per request, seed 42, temperature 0, and `ignore_eos`.

For each A/B pair, the Triton and CUDA variants use matching inputs, launch parameters, and shared runtime adaptations. Serving traces separately confirm that the intended scorer runs on all eight ranks. Benchmark revisions are A=`8a18da3b9f` and B=`a3f3ed6694`; their source difference is the nine-file CUDA increment. The shared legacy MLA compatibility and FlashInfer runtime-library selection fix are benchmark-environment adaptations, outside that increment.

The performance measurements below were collected on base `2d44b55010`, before rebasing the submission onto main `8368f86fd7`. End-to-end performance has not been remeasured on that new base.

### GPU attribution on Triton 3.6.0

Same host, batch 64, alternating A1 → B1 → A2 → B2, with a fresh server process for each capture. GPU measurements use a fixed 30-round decode window per capture, validated across all ranks for constant batch/request membership, graph execution, and no prefill, completion, or retraction in the selected window. Values below are rank-0 averages across the two captures per variant.

| Metric | Triton | CUDA | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Candidate GPU kernel time per decode round, four calls | 21.181 ms | 4.709 ms | **4.50× faster** |
| Complete GPU decode-round period | 107.354 ms | 90.293 ms | **−15.89%** |
| CPU launch interval in separate unprofiled controls | 106.957 ms | 90.168 ms | **−15.70%** |

Candidate kernels save 16.47 ms per round, compared with 17.06 ms saved over the complete GPU round. Measured overlap between candidate kernels and other GPU work is approximately 0.001 ms per round. ### Fixed-batch steady decode throughput without a profiler

One batched request is admitted at a time, with no request replenishment. The native steady throughput window runs from the last request's first token to the first request's completion, using interpolated token counts. It is distinct from full-request serving throughput.

| Baseline | Batch | Triton output tok/s | CUDA output tok/s | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Triton 3.6.0 | 8 | 1,629.07 | 1,536.89 | −5.66% |
| Triton 3.6.0 | 32 | 1,949.18 | 2,078.19 | +6.62% |
| Triton 3.6.0 | 64 | 2,693.74 | 3,149.49 | **+16.92%** |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 8 | 1,684.49 | 1,655.42 | −1.73% |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 16 | 2,189.50 | 2,404.89 | +9.84% |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 32 | 2,087.53 | 2,135.87 | +2.32%† |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 64 | 3,001.74 | 3,445.91 | **+14.80%** |

For Triton 3.6.0, each variant/shape has three measured batches across two server processes, with a full target-shape warmup before measurement in each process. The first process supplies two samples and the second supplies one; these are not three independent server restarts. The table reports per-variant medians and their ratio.

For the remaining Triton 3.7.1 batch sizes, A then B runs on the same host, with one full target-shape warmup followed by one measured batch per variant/shape. Both variants use identical CPU-only diagnostics. A separate fixed 30-round window validates constant batch/request membership, CUDA Graph execution, and no prefill, completion, or retraction across all eight ranks. At batch 64, the CPU-observed launch interval falls from 90.25 to 82.10 ms (−9.03%), while tokens/request-round increase from 4.1302 to 4.2552 (+3.03%). These intervals are not GPU kernel runtimes or client request TPOT.

**Batch 32 (†) exhibits substantial acceptance-length and throughput variation; the cause remains unresolved.** In addition to the initial pair, two paired repeats used fresh servers in B2 → A2 → A3 → B3 order, each with a full batch-32 warmup. All three pairs show shorter fixed-window CPU launch intervals: reductions of 5.60%, 6.24%, and 8.78%, with median intervals of 58.58 → 54.93 ms (−6.24%). However, fixed-window acceptance changes by −8.80%, −6.38%, and +20.56%, while native steady throughput changes by −5.74%, −0.08%, and +27.71%. The median paired throughput change is −0.08%; the marked +2.32% in the table is the ratio of per-variant medians and does not establish a consistent throughput gain. All runs are retained; the current result is an observed reduction in decode round intervals, with unstable throughput and acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Triton 3.7.1 batch-32 paired results</summary>

| Pair | Output tok/s, Triton → CUDA | Change | CPU round interval change | Fixed-window tokens/request-round, Triton → CUDA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2,265.98 → 2,135.87 | −5.74% | −5.60% | 4.8438 → 4.4177 |
| 2 | 2,087.53 → 2,085.77 | −0.08% | −6.24% | 4.4719 → 4.1865 |
| 3 | 1,906.98 → 2,435.37 | +27.71% | −8.78% | 4.0271 → 4.8552 |

Pair 1 measured batch 32 after batches 1/8/16; the added pairs measured only batch 32. Each variant had a full batch-32 warmup. All three pairs are retained. Fixed-window token counts include bonus tokens; they and the native steady throughput describe different windows and are not combined into an exact decomposition.

</details>

The two Triton campaigns do not isolate the compiler-version effect. Retractions outside the validated fixed decode windows are retained in the logs.

| Baseline | CC | Output tok/s, Triton → CUDA | Change | Mean TPOT, Triton → CUDA | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Triton 3.6.0 | 32 | 307.76 → 327.22 | +6.32% | 90.51 → 85.92 ms | −5.07% |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 32 | 319.44 → 329.16 | +3.04% | 87.14 → 85.42 ms | −1.97% |
| Triton 3.7.1 | 64 | 325.21 → 337.03 | +3.64% | 160.62 → 154.60 ms | −3.75% |

- [x] Run repository pre-commit checks on all changed files in the rebased submission branch.
- [ ] Resolve the known top-k difference's acceptance and model-level validation before merge.
- [ ] Complete upstream CI and maintainer review on the final submission revision.

+"""SM90 CUDA scorer for the paged FP4 candidate indexer.
+
+This entry point implements the H32/D128 ABI without a slots-map allocation.
+It uses natural D128 BF16 MMA operands. It preserves
+scale FTZ and BF16 rounding sites but changes K accumulation order relative to
+the pinned parity-split Triton 3.5.1 reference at commit 349c1b11c7. Numerical
+and top-k acceptance require independent oracle gates; bitwise parity is not
+promised.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once, load_jit
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_fp4_candidate_module():
+    return load_jit(
+        "dpsk_v4_fp4_index_logits_candidates_cuda",
+        cuda_files=["deepseek_v4/fp4_indexer_candidates.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[("run", "FP4IndexerCandidatesKernel::run")],
+        extra_dependencies=["cutlass"],
+    )
+
+
+def is_fp4_index_logits_candidates_cuda_supported(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    req: torch.Tensor,
+    req_table: torch.Tensor,
+    lens: torch.Tensor,
+    table: torch.Tensor,
+    page_size: int,
+    max_len: int,
+    ratio: int,
+    blocks: torch.Tensor,
+) -> bool:
+    """Check host metadata only, including layouts normalized by the wrapper.
+
+    Arbitrary positive page sizes, padded cache/request rows, strided inputs
+    and unaligned storage offsets retain the support of the original kernel.
+    Request IDs and mapped slots must be valid, as for the Triton scorer.
+    """
+    if not q.is_cuda or torch.version.hip is not None:
+        return False
+    if q.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or q.ndim != 3 or q.shape[1:] != (32, 128):
+        return False
+    batch = q.shape[0]
+    if weights.shape != (batch, 32) or req.shape != (batch,) or lens.shape != (batch,):
+        return False
+    if table.dtype != torch.uint8 or table.ndim != 2 or table.stride(1) != 1:
+        return False
+    if not 0 < page_size <= 0x7FFFFFFF or table.shape[1] != page_size * 68:
+        return False
+    if req_table.ndim != 2 or req_table.stride(1) != 1:
+        return False
+    if ratio not in (1, 2) or not 0 <= max_len <= req_table.shape[1] // ratio:
+        return False
+    if blocks.ndim != 2 or blocks.shape[0] != batch:
+        return False
+    if any(
+        t.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64)
+        for t in (req, req_table, lens, blocks)
+    ):
+        return False
+    if any(
+        t.device != q.device for t in (weights, req, req_table, lens, table, blocks)
+    ):
+        return False
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_capability(q.device) == (9, 0)
+
+
+def fp4_index_logits_candidates_cuda(

+    weights: torch.Tensor,

+    table: torch.Tensor,

+"""Independent test data and FP64 interval oracle for compact FP4 scores.
+
+No production decode/score helper is used by the oracle. The two visible BF16
+rounds and final BF16 round are explicit. FP32 dot uncertainty is bounded by
+gamma(128)*sum(abs(q*k)); head reduction by gamma(31)*sum(abs(weighted)).
+These standard rounding bounds cover either parity accumulation order and any
+FP32 reduction tree, for these finite, nonoverflowing normal-range fixtures.
+Monotone BF16 rounding propagates interval endpoints through each round; signed
+weights swap endpoints. Exact analytic cases additionally require zero error.
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+SEED = 40860
+SUPPORTED_TOPK = (512, 1024)
+GATES = {
+    "cuda_triton": "FP64 interval and full-row selection contract; bitwise delta reported; optional require_bitwise parity gate; exact -inf mask",
+    "oracle": "FP64 full dot with explicit BF16 rounds; propagated gamma128/gamma31 interval",
+    "analytic": "exact scores and masks",
+    "topk": "512/1024 on every row/all candidates; exact higher-than-cutoff membership; equal-cutoff alternatives accepted",
+    "no_post_result_relaxation": True,
+    "reference_semantics_erratum": "Before CUDA testing: Triton SM90 exp2 FTZ maps exponent byte0 to scale0; mathematical UE8M0 remains2^-127, recorded separately",
+    "fixture_domain": "H32 D128, finite BF16 Q/W; random K exponents119..135 plus analytic0/27/127/227; no overflow",
+}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Inputs:
+    q: torch.Tensor
+    weights: torch.Tensor
+    req: torch.Tensor
+    req_table: torch.Tensor
+    lens: torch.Tensor
+    table: torch.Tensor
+    page_size: int
+    max_len: int
+    ratio: int
+    blocks: torch.Tensor
+
+    def args(self):
+        return (
+            self.q,
+            self.weights,
+            self.req,
+            self.req_table,
+            self.lens,
+            self.table,
+            self.page_size,
+            self.max_len,
+            self.ratio,
+            self.blocks,
+        )
+
+    def bytes(self):
+        return sum(
+            x.numel() * x.element_size()
+            for x in self.args()
+            if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)
+        )
+
+
+def implementations(baseline_only=False):
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.fp4_indexer import (
+        fp4_index_logits_candidates_triton,
+    )
+
+    if baseline_only or os.environ.get("FP4_CANDIDATE_TEST_IMPL") == "triton":
+        return {"triton": fp4_index_logits_candidates_triton}
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.fp4_indexer_cuda import (
+        fp4_index_logits_candidates_cuda,
+    )
+
+    return {
+        "triton": fp4_index_logits_candidates_triton,
+        "cuda": fp4_index_logits_candidates_cuda,
+    }
+
+
+def make_inputs(
+    requests=2,
+    queries=2,
+    candidates=72,
+    *,
+    max_len=137,
+    ratio=1,
+    mapping="random",
+    q_kind="arbitrary",
+    dtype=torch.int32,
+    padded=False,
+    seed=SEED,
+    device="cuda",
+    analytic=False,
+    strided=False,
+):
+    assert candidates % 8 == 0
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    rows, page_size = requests * queries, 64
+    slots_per_req = math.ceil(max(max_len, 1) / page_size) * page_size
+    slots = requests * slots_per_req
+    pages = slots // page_size
+    # Guard bytes survive H2D and expose incorrect cache stride assumptions.
+    backing = torch.full(
+        (pages, page_size * 68 + (37 if padded else 0)), 0xA5, dtype=torch.uint8
+    )
+    table = backing[:, : page_size * 68]
+    payload = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (pages, page_size * 64), generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8
+    )
+    exps = torch.randint(
+        119, 136, (pages, page_size * 4), generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8
+    )
+    table[:, : page_size * 64] = payload
+    table[:, page_size * 64 :] = exps
+    q = torch.randn(rows, 32, 128, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = (torch.randn(rows, 32, generator=g) / 32).to(torch.bfloat16)

+    if rows:
+        q[0, 0] = 0
+        weights[0, 1:3] = torch.tensor([1.0, -1.0], dtype=torch.bfloat16)

+        (requests, max_len * ratio + (19 if padded else 0)), -31337, dtype=dtype
+    )
+    req_table = tb[:, : max_len * ratio]
+    for r in range(requests):
+        physical = torch.arange(r * slots_per_req, (r + 1) * slots_per_req)
+        if mapping == "random":
+            physical = physical[torch.randperm(slots_per_req, generator=g)]
+        req_table[r, ::ratio] = physical[:max_len].to(dtype) * ratio
+    lens = torch.full((rows,), max_len, dtype=dtype)
+    nblocks = candidates // 8
+    blocks = torch.empty((rows, nblocks), dtype=dtype)
+    for row in range(rows):
+        block_ids = torch.arange(max(1, math.ceil(max_len / 8)))
+        if mapping == "random":
+            block_ids = block_ids[torch.randperm(block_ids.numel(), generator=g)]

+        blocks[row] = block_ids.roll(row % max(block_ids.numel(), 1)).repeat(
+            math.ceil(nblocks / max(block_ids.numel(), 1))
+        )[:nblocks]

+        table[:, : page_size * 64] = 0
+        table[:, page_size * 64 :] = 127
+        # First K coordinate cycles through exactly representable E2M1 values.
+        table[:, : page_size * 64].reshape(pages, page_size, 64)[:, :, 0] = (
+            torch.arange(slots).reshape(pages, page_size).remainder(8).byte()
+        )
+        q.zero_()
+        weights.zero_()
+        if rows:
+            q[:, 0, 0] = 1
+            weights[:, 0] = 1
+
+    def transfer(x):
+        if padded and x is table:
+            return backing.to(device)[:, : page_size * 68]
+        if padded and x is req_table:
+            return tb.to(device)[:, : max_len * ratio]
+        return x.to(device)
+
+    result = Inputs(
+        *(transfer(x) for x in (q, weights, req, req_table, lens, table)),
+        page_size,
+        max_len,
+        ratio,
+        transfer(blocks),

+    if q_kind == "fakequant":
+        # Exercise the actual production query preparation; oracle is independent.
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.fp4_fake_quant import fake_quant_fp4
+
+        result.q = fake_quant_fp4(result.q)
+    if strided:
+        for name in ("q", "weights", "req", "lens", "blocks"):
+            x = getattr(result, name)
+            bigger = torch.empty(
+                (*x.shape[:-1], x.shape[-1] * 2), dtype=x.dtype, device=device
+            )
+            bigger[..., ::2].copy_(x)
+            setattr(result, name, bigger[..., ::2])

+def coordinates(inputs):
+    blocks = inputs.blocks.cpu().long()
+    logical = (blocks[:, :, None] * 8 + torch.arange(8)).flatten(1)
+    valid = (
+        (blocks.repeat_interleave(8, 1) >= 0)
+        & (logical < inputs.lens.cpu().long()[:, None])
+        & (logical < inputs.max_len)
+    )
+    slots = torch.zeros_like(logical)
+    if valid.any():
+        rows = inputs.req.cpu().long()[:, None].expand_as(logical)
+        slots[valid] = (
+            inputs.req_table.cpu().long()[rows[valid], logical[valid] * inputs.ratio]
+            // inputs.ratio
+        )
+    return logical, slots, valid
+
+
+def decode_slots(table, slots, page_size, *, reference_ftz=True):
+    """Explicit layout and 16-entry E2M1 LUT, independent of Triton helpers."""
+    lut = torch.tensor(
+        [
+            0.0,
+            0.5,
+            1.0,
+            1.5,
+            2.0,
+            3.0,
+            4.0,
+            6.0,
+            -0.0,
+            -0.5,
+            -1.0,
+            -1.5,
+            -2.0,
+            -3.0,
+            -4.0,
+            -6.0,
+        ],
+        dtype=torch.float64,
+    )
+    table = table.cpu()
+    page, off = slots // page_size, slots % page_size
+    packed = table[page[:, None], off[:, None] * 64 + torch.arange(64)].long()
+    codes = torch.stack((packed & 15, packed >> 4), -1).flatten(1)
+    exp = table[
+        page[:, None], page_size * 64 + off[:, None] * 4 + torch.arange(4)
+    ].long()
+    scale = torch.pow(2.0, exp.double() - 127)

+    # Triton-only magnitude2/Q2^100 probe before any CUDA acceptance run.
+    # Mathematical UE8M0 byte0 is2^-127; SM90 ex2.approx.ftz flushes that scale.
+    if reference_ftz:
+        scale = torch.where(exp == 0, 0.0, scale)
+    scale = scale.repeat_interleave(32, 1)
+    return (lut[codes] * scale).to(torch.bfloat16).double()

+def bf16(x):
+    return x.to(torch.bfloat16).double()

+    for i, row in enumerate(rows):

+def oracle(q, keys, weights, blocks, lens):
+    positions = (
+        blocks.long()[:, :, None] * 8 + torch.arange(8, device=q.device)
+    ).flatten(1)
+    valid = (positions >= 0) & (positions < keys.shape[0]) & (positions < lens[:, None])
+    out = torch.full(positions.shape, -torch.inf, device=q.device)
+    # Bound reference memory, independently of the tested Triton tile size.
+    if keys.shape[0] and positions.shape[1]:
+        for lo in range(0, q.shape[0], 4):
+            p = positions[lo : lo + 4]
+            k = keys[p.clamp(0, keys.shape[0] - 1)]
+            dots = torch.einsum("rhd,rnd->rhn", q[lo : lo + 4], k)
+            out[lo : lo + 4] = (
+                (dots.relu() * weights[lo : lo + 4, :, None]).sum(1).float()
+            )
+    return out.masked_fill(~valid, -torch.inf), positions, valid
+

+def inputs(rows, length, count, *, strided=False, dyadic=False):
+    torch.manual_seed(431 + rows + length)

+        :, ::factor
+    ]
+    w = torch.randn(rows, 32 * factor, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)[:, ::factor]
+    if dyadic:
+        # Exact binary products/sums avoid masking a numeric discrepancy with tolerance.
+        q.copy_(q.round().clamp(-2, 2) / 8)
+        k.copy_(k.round().clamp(-2, 2) / 8)
+        w.copy_(w.round().clamp(-2, 2) / 8)
+    blocks = torch.randint(
+        -1,
+        max(2, (length + 7) // 8 + 2),
+        (rows, count * factor),
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+    )[:, ::factor]
+    lens = torch.full((rows,), length, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    if rows > 1:
+        lens[0] = 0
+        lens[1] = max(0, length - 3)
